findings.where: Hero, the identity block under the name (desktop and phone first screen)
findings.fault: The page shows nothing of Mark himself. There is no photograph, and the tile has no place where a real portrait would sit in this look. Next to the name is a circled "A", a section callout, which reads like an initial-letter avatar standing in for a missing profile picture.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staffer checking whether a real, named person is behind the advice (first-visit trust item 1; client value 3, "the man himself"). They see an empty-avatar sign instead of a face. Mark would object too, since the brief makes the individual the brand.

findings.where: Hero, the role line under the name: "LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS", and the title-block cells "DRAWING MMM-GA-001" and "SCALE NTS" in the nav bar
findings.fault: The lines that should say who Mark is and how to reach him carry drawing jargon. The second half of the role line is a drawing label, not a fact about Mark. The title block was meant to carry the nav and the contact, but its cells hold a made-up drawing number and "not to scale".
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development agency. In the 5-second read they meet codes they can't decode where they expected his role and contact. Mark would object because the direction card promised the title block would carry the contact.

findings.where: Hero, the "Write to Mark" button, and the page's end (no footer); the nav's CONTACT link
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto button. Mark's email address never appears as text anywhere on the page, and the sheet ends with no footer holding the address, base country or regions of work.
findings.who_objects: A bank staffer on a work machine with webmail or a locked-down mail client. Clicking the button opens nothing useful, and they have no address to copy into a procurement shortlist (first-visit trust items 6 and 7).

findings.where: Hero, the statement on the right: "…with over 40 years of international infrastructure experience"
findings.fault: Mark's standing rests on a size claim ("over 40 years") instead of checkable work. The World Bank PPP Group role, which a reader can check, sits next to it and is weakened by it.
findings.who_objects: Procurement-minded readers, who judge relevant experience by named bodies, roles and regions, not by years. Mark would object too: the brief asks for "confident without big-firm claims, no boasts", and the house rule bans size words like "40 years of experience".

findings.where: Hero, the statement and role line (5-second test)
findings.fault: Above the fold the page says what Mark does, but not who it is for. Development banks, agencies and governments are never named, and the article specimen is the first place a "development agency" client appears.
findings.who_objects: A multilateral-bank staffer deciding in seconds whether this advisor works for organisations like theirs (first-visit trust: "what a visitor must be sure of" for an advisor).

findings.where: Article specimen, the related-lecture row "Streamlining the PPP Process… · Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF"
findings.fault: The talk row's format has no venue or host. A lecture shows standing only through where it was given, and the layout round will copy this row as the pattern for every talk.
findings.who_objects: A visitor weighing Mark's standing. Being asked to speak by a named body is the proof (feel the CV: the newest talk with its venue), and this row leaves it out.

findings.where: Whole page, from the hero down to the end
findings.fault: There is no third-party proof anywhere, not even a link out to work a named body hosts, such as a World Bank publication or the lecture's host page.
findings.who_objects: A cautious first-time visitor from a development agency, who has only Mark's own word for his standing (first-visit trust item 14; with no testimonials held, a link to work a named body hosts is the honest proof).
